title: T1565.001 — Data Manipulation - Stored Data Manipulation
subtitle: Watch an attacker who is already inside the network move to the database host, change stored balances, and attack the audit trail.
aria: T1565.001 - Data Manipulation - Stored Data Manipulation

nodes.label: Sensitive data
nodes.tip: Sensitive data - What is at risk

steps.title: Lateral move to the DB host
steps.caption: The attacker already controls a file server (FS-03) through a stolen service account. From there, they reach FIN-DB-01, the host running the finance database, using admin access that the account should never have had.
steps.defender: an off-hours network logon on FIN-DB-01, sourced from FS-03, not from the application tier.

detection.label: No detection
detection.detail: This activity is not visible to the victim yet.

steps.title: UPDATE the balances table
steps.caption: The attacker opens a SQL client and runs an UPDATE statement that rewrites the balance column for a customer account. The stored value changes permanently.
steps.defender: the database activity monitor captures the statement, because it ships audit rows off the host in near real time.

detection.label: No detection
detection.detail: This activity is not visible to the victim yet.

steps.title: Edit and delete audit rows
steps.caption: To hide the change, the attacker deletes rows from the local audit table and removes the audit log files on the host.
steps.defender: the local audit trail goes quiet - but the copy already shipped to the monitor still exists.

steps.title: SIEM raises a log-gap alert
steps.caption: The SIEM expects a steady stream from FIN-DB-01. When the stream stops during business hours, a gap alert fires. Silence is treated as a signal, not as peace
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: The database activity monitor flags the UPDATE
steps.caption: Because the monitor received the audit rows before deletion, it can still alert on the direct UPDATE from a non-application user. Two independent views of the same write now exist
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: FIM shows a changed config under /etc
steps.caption: File integrity monitoring reports that /etc/my.cnf on the DB host left its baseline - the attacker tried to weaken the audit plugin settings for the next boot. FIM proves the file-level edit even without host logs
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: The analyst compares last good backup with current data
steps.caption: The analyst pulls the last known-good backup and diffs the balances table. The diff shows exactly which rows changed, when, and by which session - this scopes the incident and becomes evidence
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.caption: The team restores the changed rows from the trusted backup, rotates the stolen credentials, re-enables and protects the audit configuration so it cannot be switched off silently, and fixes the preconditions: least privilege on the DB host, MFA on admin paths, and FIM coverage on the config files
